note: Hand-scored by Claude from public commentary found via web search on 2026-11-13, using the rubric in collector/giq/commentary.py. Where a house gave no number the score is a judgment call; see scoring_rationale. Dates marked 'approx' could not be confirmed.

views.title: US Market Pulse — November 2026
views.summary: Resilient growth (~2.5% in 2027) backed by balance sheets, AI capex and fiscal cushions; expects a December Fed hike, then data-dependent — a hold at 4.0–4.25% if energy/tariff impulses roll off.
key_points: Fed hike expected in December; March data-dependent
Inflation seen normalizing as energy and tariff impulses fade
Earnings growth slows in 2027 but still supports equities
quotes: We expect 2027 growth near 2.5% in the US, and above 1% in Europe and Japan.
We expect them to raise rates in December, but the move in March will be highly dependent on the data.
views.scoring_rationale: Growth 2.5% - 2.0 trend = +0.5 (explicit). No core PCE number; 'normalizing' from ~3.1% core PCE implies ~2.7% average over 12m -> +0.7 with qualitative sd 0.6.

views.title: Midterms and AI in focus at 2027 Forum (Weekly commentary)
views.summary: Persistent inflation pressures keep Fed-hike expectations alive, but BII thinks further hikes are over-priced (overweight short Treasuries). Key growth risk: an AI-capex slowdown in 2027. Supply-driven regime 'largely priced in'.
key_points: Persistent inflation pressures; inflation settles above pre-pandemic levels
Market pricing of further Fed hikes looks excessive
A material AI-spending slowdown in 2027 is the main downside risk
Downgraded US equities to neutral in October
quotes: We expect persistent inflation pressures to keep market expectations for further Fed rate hikes alive.
The supply-driven regime we've described for five years is largely priced in, making the outlook less directional.
views.scoring_rationale: Qualitative only. Inflation 'persistent/sticky above target' = +1.0. Growth resilient near term but stresses 2027 slowdown risk -> +0.3 with sd 0.8+0.2 for tail emphasis.

views.title: Growth Holds, Risks Widen (Cyclical Outlook)
views.summary: Benign base case: resilient global growth over 6–12 months and inflation moderating as the energy shock fades, with only modest spillover to core and wages. Central banks unlikely to deliver all priced hikes. Wide tails: AI slowdown, worse energy shock, tighter financial conditions.
key_points: Growth resilient over the cyclical horizon
Inflation moderates as energy shock fades
Fed/others won't need to fully deliver priced hikes
quotes: we expect global growth to remain resilient over our six- to 12-month cyclical horizon
inflation moderates as the energy price shock fades
views.scoring_rationale: Qualitative. Resilient growth -> +0.4; 'moderating toward target' -> +0.6. sd widened (+0.2) because the piece stresses fat tails.

views.title: Vanguard economic and market outlook — United States
views.summary: Raised year-end 2026 core PCE forecast to 3.2%, expects tariff effects to fade so core PCE moves toward 2.5% by April 2027; adds one more Fed hike in early 2027. Ex-supply factors, underlying inflation is near 2%.
key_points: Year-end 2026 core PCE forecast raised to 3.2%
One more Fed hike anticipated in early 2027
quotes: prompting us to recently raise our year-end 2026 core inflation forecast to 3.2%
Excluding those supply factors, underlying inflation is much closer to the Fed's 2% target.
views.scoring_rationale: Core PCE path 3.2% -> 2.5% averages ~2.8% over 12m -> +0.8 (explicit, sd 0.35). GDP 2.3%/3.0% figure could not be dated -> +0.6 with sd 0.6.

views.title: Monthly Economic Outlook — November 2026
views.summary: Real GDP 2.5% Q4/Q4 in 2026 slowing to 2.0% in 2027; core PCE 3.2% y/y in Q4 2026 easing to 2.5% by end-2027; two more 25bp hikes by early 2027 to 4.25–4.50%; 25% recession probability.
key_points: Two more Fed hikes by early 2027 (4.25–4.50%)
quotes: We expect core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation to average 3.2% year-over-year in Q4 2026
We maintain a 25% probability of recession over the next 12 months.
views.scoring_rationale: Next-4-quarter growth ~2.15% -> +0.15; core PCE averaging ~2.85% over the horizon -> +0.85. Point forecasts (sd 0.3) widened on growth for the 25% recession tail.

views.title: 2026 Midterms: economic implications (approx. date)
views.summary: Headline CPI ends 2026 at 3.6% and slows only to 3.0% by end-2027; AI investment, energy and consumer resilience drive the outlook. Mid-year WFII targets: GDP 2.2% (2026), 2.4% (2027).
quotes: We expect 12-month topline Consumer Price Index inflation to end 2027 at 3.0%, slowing only modestly from our year-end 2026 forecast of 3.6%.
views.scoring_rationale: CPI path minus 0.4 CPI/PCE wedge -> ~2.9% core-PCE-equivalent average -> +0.9. Growth from June WFII targets (older) -> +0.3 with sd 0.6. Publication date approximate.

views.title: Fed hike outlook raised to 4.25–4.5% terminal (via secondary coverage)
views.summary: After the September hike, MS expects two more (December, March) to a 4.25–4.5% terminal rate as energy-driven inflation persists; Gapen: economy can absorb 75–100bp of hikes. Mid-year GDP path 2.25% (2026), 2.5% (2027).
key_points: Inflation decline slower than Fed wants
quotes: economy can handle 75-100 bps in total hikes
views.scoring_rationale: Growth from May outlook (2.25-2.5%) -> +0.35. Inflation 'persistent, more hikes needed' -> +1.1. Low confidence: latest view partly from secondary coverage.

views.title: Bowman: The US economy and considerations for monetary policy
views.summary: Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman: Q3 GDP likely >3% after 2.4% in H1, driven by AI capex and consumers; core PCE ~3.3% in October; labor market stable but not tight (~80k jobs/month, 4.1% unemployment). Expects core PCE to move closer to 2% next year; further tightening must be weighed against costs.
key_points: Policy not on a preset course
quotes: my forecast is for core PCE inflation to move closer to 2 percent next year.
our progress on lowering inflation has disappointed.
views.scoring_rationale: One FOMC voter, not the Committee. Strong current growth but no forward number -> +0.5. Core PCE 3.3% falling 'closer to 2%' -> ~2.6% average -> +0.6.

views.title: Economic trends: mid-year update (Commercial Banking)
views.summary: July view: 2026 GDP 1.5–2.0%; year-end core PCE raised to 3.4% (from 2.9%) on the Strait of Hormuz energy/fertilizer shock; Fed on hold at 3.50–3.75%. Superseded by events (Fed hiked in September).
quotes: Our outlook for core PCE at year end is now 3.4%, up from 2.9% at the beginning of the year.
views.scoring_rationale: Stale (July). Midpoint 1.75% -> -0.25; core PCE 3.4% -> +1.4. Kept to show the drift of views; down-weighted automatically.

views.title: BofA sees rising odds of US reflation mini-cycle into 2027–28 (secondary coverage)
views.summary: June 2026: rising odds of a US reflation mini-cycle lasting into 2027–28; May: no Fed cuts before H2-2027 given high inflation and positive job growth. 2027 Year Ahead not yet published.
views.scoring_rationale: Stale, qualitative, secondary source. 'Reflation' -> above-trend growth (+0.6) and above-target inflation (+1.2), wide sd.
